narration: It was a night when the stars shone beautifully. I remember a boy once standing atop a hill on a night like this. It’s a memory from so long ago that nostalgia alone can’t quite describe it.

I used to hate the night. Nightfall brought a specific kind of silence—one that felt heavy and sharp with cold. I’d slip between the frozen sheets, feeling the vast, ink-black space of the room pressing in on me. Even with my eyelids squeezed shut, the darkness felt alive, keeping rest just out of reach.  I would brace myself against the dark and pray for the morning to come.
